items.title: Louie Bellson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I enjoyed having respect for them. Francine and I looked at this television show, Bernie Mac. Bernie Mac is very talented.

ctx.x: And you’re still here, and they’re not.

Yeah. I’m still doing it. I had my apple this morning for breakfast. Taking care of yourself, and making your craft something that’s very sacred to you. We’re all drummers, and we make our drumming sacred. It’s something that we appreciate, we love, and we’re still doing. I think that, with that thought in mind, if the kids can learn that, they’ll be better off. At home, too. That word, respect – all three of us respect drumming, just like we respect our mothers and fathers. I look at television today and some of…
None of us would be here, talking to our parents like that.
